data.title: Other topical azoles: econazole, sulconazole, bifonazole
data.body:
_More from Khopkar · Topical antifungals_

**Class:** Imidazole antifungals (topical)

## Mechanism of action
- Inhibit 14-α-demethylase → ergosterol depletion; econazole and sulconazole also antibacterial (Gram-positives)
- Bifonazole also inhibits HMG-CoA reductase — stays in skin long enough for once-daily use

## Indications in dermatology & STI
- Tinea corporis, cruris, pedis; cutaneous candidiasis; pityriasis versicolor; erythrasma (econazole)
- Bifonazole 1% with 40% urea: onychomycosis (nail avulsion kit)

## Dose & formulations
- Econazole 1% once or twice daily; sulconazole 1% once or twice daily; bifonazole 1% once daily — 2–4 weeks

## Adverse effects
- Burning, itching, contact dermatitis (imidazoles cross-react)

## Contraindications
- Imidazole allergy

## Pregnancy & lactation
Minimal absorption; acceptable.

## Viva points
- Bifonazole — once daily, long skin retention
- Econazole — also antibacterial (useful in infected toe webs)

_Sources: Khopkar ch.19; Wolverton 4e ch.42. Facts summarised in our own words; Wolverton followed where books differ._
